description: Thread-safe LRU cache attempts to perform linked-list node movement under a shared read lock during `get()` calls, violating write exclusivity during node recency mutations.
spec_notes: Invariant: Any operation that mutates data structures (including LRU recency reordering) must be guarded with exclusive write locking.

from typing import Dict, Optional, Any
from node import Node
from rwlock import ReadWriteLock

class ThreadSafeLRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 3):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache: Dict[str, Node] = {}
        self.lock = ReadWriteLock()
        self.head = Node("head", None)
        self.tail = Node("tail", None)
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self.head

    def _remove(self, node: Node):
        p = node.prev
        n = node.next
        if p and n:
            p.next = n
            n.prev = p

    def _add_to_head(self, node: Node):
        node.next = self.head.next
        node.prev = self.head
        if self.head.next:
            self.head.next.prev = node
        self.head.next = node

    def get(self, key: str) -> Optional[Any]:
        # Bug: acquires read lock but mutates linked list via _remove and _add_to_head!
        self.lock.acquire_read()
        try:
            if key in self.cache:
                node = self.cache[key]
                self._remove(node)
                self._add_to_head(node)
                return node.value
            return None
        finally:
            self.lock.release_read()

    def put(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        self.lock.acquire_write()
        try:
            if key in self.cache:
                self._remove(self.cache[key])
            node = Node(key, value)
            self.cache[key] = node
            self._add_to_head(node)
            if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
                lru = self.tail.prev
                if lru and lru != self.head:
                    self._remove(lru)
                    del self.cache[lru.key]
        finally:
            self.lock.release_write()

tests.test_safe_cache.py:
from safe_cache import ThreadSafeLRUCache

def test_basic_put_get():
    cache = ThreadSafeLRUCache(capacity=2)
    cache.put("a", 1)
    cache.put("b", 2)
    assert cache.get("a") == 1
    cache.put("c", 3) # 'b' is now LRU and evicted
    assert cache.get("b") is None
    assert cache.get("a") == 1
    assert cache.get("c") == 3

def test_get_mutation_requires_write_lock():
    cache = ThreadSafeLRUCache(capacity=3)
    cache.put("k1", 100)
    # Record write acquisitions before get
    writes_before = cache.lock.write_acquisitions
    val = cache.get("k1")
    assert val == 100
    # Invariant: because get() reorders the doubly-linked list, it must acquire write lock
    assert cache.lock.write_acquisitions == writes_before + 1
